newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian appeals court upholds Craxi conviction.
newsitem.headline: Italian appeals court upholds Craxi conviction.

text.p: An Italian appeals court on Friday upheld a four-year jail sentence against former prime minister Bettino Craxi in what has become known as "the mother of all corruption trials".
The Milan court took six hours to arrive at its decision in a case that originally lasted 16 months, spearheaded by former anti-graft magistrate Antonio Di Pietro and televised across Italy.

It upheld an earlier sentence against Craxi as well as a one-year prison conviction against former interior minister Claudio Martelli, who was a prominent member of the Socialist Party which Craxi led.
The Enimont trial was the single most important case to emerge from the vast "Clean Hands" graft investigations led by Di Pietro which toppled Italy's corrupt political old guard.
It involved the chemical company Montedison, which paid more than $100 million in kickbacks to extricate itself from a disastrous joint venture with state energy company ENI.

Last month, the Milan court upheld sentences against top politicians including former prime minister Aldo Forlani and Northern League secessionist leader Umberto Bossi, who had been found guilty of illegal party financing in the Enimont trial.
The court had separately considered the case of Martelli and Craxi, who has chalked up several convictions for corruption and lives in self-imposed exile in Tunisia.
All the convicted parties are eligible for one last appeal to Italy's highest court, the Cassation Court.
